chunks: From him, from Mūsā ibn ʿUmar, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Mīthamī, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, from his grandfather, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a well into which a mouse or some other animal falls and dies, and dough is kneaded from its water: may that bread be eaten? He said, “If the fire has reached it, then there is no harm in eating it.”

key_terms.الدَّوَابِّ: animals or crawling creatures other than the mouse
key_terms.النَّارُ: fire, referring to the baking or cooking process
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.الْخُبْزُ: the bread made from dough kneaded with that water
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةُ: a mouse, given as the example of an animal falling into the well
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection in the legal sense
key_terms.مَائِهَا: its water, meaning the water of the well

ai.seo_question: Can bread made with water from a well in which a dead mouse fell be eaten?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding bread made with water from a well in which a mouse or another animal died. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that if the bread was affected by fire, there is no problem in eating it, indicating a ruling tied to cooking by fire in this case.
